initial.name: Compromised Trusted Relationship
initial.description: The attackers exploited a relationship between your organization and a third-party (e.g., vendor, partner, contractor) that has a service-level account within your organization and gained unauthorized access.

pivot.name: Kerberoasting
pivot.description: The attackers compromise additional systems by using a “feature” of Service Principal Names (SPNs) to extract and crack service passwords.

c2.name: Domain Fronting as C2
c2.description: The attackers route requests destined for their server through legitimate web services like Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).

persist.name: Malicious Service
persist.description: The attackers create or modify system services in order to maintain long-term access to a compromised system.

procedures.name: Server Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders monitor sever activity, logs, and configurations to detect abnormal behaviors, such as unauthorized access, unusual traffic, or process anomalies.

procedures.name: Firewall Log Review
procedures.description: Can your organization analyze and understand firewall logs? Do you regularly emulate attack scenarios and verify that your procedures work?

procedures.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders monitor, collect and examine event logs generated by cloud-based systems and services to identify potential security incidents, misconfigurations , and unusual or unauthorized activities.

procedures.name: Crisis Management
procedures.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

procedures.name: Active Defense and Cyber Deception
procedures.description: The Defenders simulate real systems and services, luring attackers to interact with them, carefully monitoring and alerting on those interactions.

procedures.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders use SIEM to aggregate logs from systems and devices to identify abnormal patterns, such as unusual access, traffic, or attack signatures.

procedures.name: Isolation
procedures.description: The Defenders quarantine compromised systems or network segments to prevent further spread of malicious activity, containing threats while enabling secure investigation and remediation.

metadata.name: Vendor Veil APT Campaign
metadata.author: JonesCKevin
metadata.description: An advanced persistent threat actor leverages a compromised supply chain partner to infiltrate the target network, escalates via Active Directory abuse, and maintains stealthy long-term access.

notes: The APT first abuses a trusted vendor relationship to gain initial foothold. Once inside, the attacker performs Kerberoasting to harvest service account credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation. Command and control is established via domain fronting to blend with legitimate cloud traffic. Persistence is achieved by registering a malicious service that survives reboots and provides ongoing access.
